summary: Assess SOE, PPP, and guarantee exposures with practical fiscal-risk tools. Build a register and budget-linked scenarios. Explore the five-day course.
lede: Fiscal risk analysis helps public finance teams assess how state-owned enterprises, public-private partnerships and guarantees could affect budgets. It is for treasury and finance officials, debt analysts, PPP specialists, public investment managers and auditors who need to map exposures and support budget decisions. Participants practise classifying liabilities, maintaining spreadsheet-based risk registers, testing baseline and downside scenarios, and preparing fiscal-risk reports with documented assumptions and mitigation actions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for public finance professionals who assess fiscal exposures, oversee public entities or infrastructure projects, and prepare analysis for budget and accountability processes. This course is designed for: Treasury fiscal-risk analysts who maintain registers of contingent liabilities. Finance-ministry budget officers who assess fiscal exposures in budget submissions. Public debt analysts who evaluate guarantees and government payment obligations. PPP unit analysts who screen projects using PFRAM. Public investment managers who review project risks and fiscal affordability. SOE financial-monitoring officers who assess entity performance and government exposure. Government auditors who examine fiscal-risk controls and reporting evidence. Budget directors who incorporate fiscal-risk analysis into budget decisions. Public-sector accountants who classify contingent liabilities in fiscal reports. Development finance advisers who support government fiscal-risk analysis and reporting.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with public budgeting, fiscal reporting, public debt, public investment, or PPP processes is recommended. No programming is required. Bring a basic understanding of your agency’s fiscal-risk or budget processes; exercises use structured case information and spreadsheet-based analysis.
